title: BBC Ghosts from the Past
paragraphs: A BBC supernatural-drama collection of ghost stories dramatized for radio, presented here as a small group of eerie standalone plays.
Four-part BBC Radio 4 supernatural-drama anthology directed by Martin Jenkins. Frozen GRH set contains the complete four-program April 1992 run.
GRH documents the program through BBC Radio 4 April 1992 run (April 8, 1992 to April 29, 1992) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Martin Jenkins (director on 4 recordings), Brett Usher (performer on 2 recordings), David Learner (performer on 2 recordings), Eric Allan (performer on 2 recordings), Gudrun Ure (performer on 2 recordings), Ann Windsor (performer on 1 recording), and Benjamin Whitrow (performer on 1 recording).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include ghosts and supernatural haunting, memory, guilt and the return of the past, M. R. James and antiquarian ghost-story tradition, marriage, death and obsessive possession, and Oxbridge academic supernatural setting.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including BBC Radio 4 Ghosts from the Past run and Modern BBC revival of the literary ghost-play tradition.
plain_text:
A BBC supernatural-drama collection of ghost stories dramatized for radio, presented here as a small group of eerie standalone plays.

Four-part BBC Radio 4 supernatural-drama anthology directed by Martin Jenkins. Frozen GRH set contains the complete four-program April 1992 run.

GRH documents the program through BBC Radio 4 April 1992 run (April 8, 1992 to April 29, 1992) on BBC Radio 4.

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Martin Jenkins (director on 4 recordings), Brett Usher (performer on 2 recordings), David Learner (performer on 2 recordings), Eric Allan (performer on 2 recordings), Gudrun Ure (performer on 2 recordings), Ann Windsor (performer on 1 recording), and Benjamin Whitrow (performer on 1 recording).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include ghosts and supernatural haunting, memory, guilt and the return of the past, M. R. James and antiquarian ghost-story tradition, marriage, death and obsessive possession, and Oxbridge academic supernatural setting.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including BBC Radio 4 Ghosts from the Past run and Modern BBC revival of the literary ghost-play tradition.
